title: Why Does an Exchange Ask Who Owns the Wallet Before a Crypto Swap?
keyQuestions: Why does an exchange ask who owns the destination wallet?
Is a crypto swap deposit address considered a personal wallet?
Does a wallet ownership question mean the swap requires KYC?
How should a service-controlled swap deposit address be classified?
What verification methods can prove control of a self-custody wallet?
Can wallet verification or address whitelisting make a swap quote expire?
Should funds be withdrawn to a personal wallet before opening a swap order?
quickSteps: Classify the destination as your wallet, another person's wallet, or a service-controlled address before opening the withdrawal form.
Verify the source platform's beneficiary and wallet ownership requirements before creating a time-sensitive swap order.
Select the destination category accurately and never claim control of private keys you do not hold.
Complete only the official verification method that matches the destination type, without sharing wallet secrets.
Create a fresh swap order and send funds only after the withdrawal path, network, amount, and address are ready.

issueRouting.start: The source platform asks who owns the destination address before releasing a crypto withdrawal.

branches.if: The destination is a self-custody wallet controlled by the user
then: Select the personal or self-hosted wallet category.
Complete the platform's official proof-of-control method if requested.
Confirm that the verification request does not include token approvals or unrelated contract actions.

branches.if: The destination belongs to another person or a hosted account
then: Choose the beneficiary or hosted-provider category that matches the destination.
Provide the requested beneficiary or receiving-platform information accurately.
Do not enter the sender's details as the wallet owner unless they are also the real beneficiary.

branches.if: The destination is a temporary address issued by a crypto swap service
then: Classify it as a service-controlled, hosted, business, or other-provider address when an accurate option exists.
Use the receiving service's real name if the withdrawal form requests it.
Ask the source platform's official support for classification guidance if no available option describes the address.

riskNotes: Creating a swap order does not give the user private-key control of the service's deposit address.
A proof-of-control request may be impossible for a temporary address operated by the receiving swap service.
Manual review, address whitelisting, or a cooling-off period can outlast a time-sensitive swap quote.
Old deposit addresses should not be reused because a new order may have different route, amount, memo, or address requirements.
Wallet ownership verification never requires a seed phrase, private key, keystore file, backup, or remote device access.
A no-registration swap does not erase identity and withdrawal records already retained by the source exchange.
